Features of a private, local AI coder

  • Private, local AI

    The model runs on your PC with llama.cpp. Your code, chats and history never leave your computer. No account, no telemetry.

  • Works offline

    After a one-time model download, everything works without the internet: on a plane, on a locked-down network or with Wi-Fi off.

  • Agent with file and command tools

    The assistant can list, read and search files, propose edits and run commands in your project. Every change shows a diff and waits for your approval, with automatic backups and undo.

  • Project code search

    Open any folder. Offline Coder indexes your code and finds matches with file and line numbers, so answers are grounded in your actual project.

  • Qwen3 models picked by RAM

    It checks your memory and graphics card and recommends Qwen3 8B, Qwen3 4B Instruct 2507 or Llama 3.2 3B. Switch models any time.

  • Auto-tune for your PC

    Re-tune for this PC benchmarks your hardware and picks the fastest engine (Vulkan GPU or CPU), context size and threads.

  • Voice input

    Click Voice, speak, click Stop. Speech recognition runs locally with whisper.cpp, so your voice stays on your PC too.

  • Knowledge library import

    Import your official ChatGPT, Grok or Claude export, or a folder of notes, so answers can draw on your own past conversations. Stored locally.

  • 30 specialist bots that work together

    Coding: ProgrammingBot, ArchitectBot, EditorBot, ToolsmithBot (builds its own tools for bulk edits), ReviewBot, DebugBot, TestBot, SecurityBot, DocsBot, WebBot, PythonBot, CppBot, CSharpBot, RustGoBot, MobileBot, ShellBot, SQLBot, DataBot, SEOBot, GameDevBot and BlenderBot. Design: DesignBot (palettes, logos and icons as SVG) and WebDesignBot. Business: ExcelBot, AutomationBot, WriterBot, EmailBot, MarketingBot, FinanceBot and SupportBot. Any bot can ask another for a second opinion, so the Python bot can get a schema from the SQL bot. Leave it on Auto and each message goes to the best bot automatically, or lock one in.

  • A real agent workflow

    A visible task plan, project notes it remembers between chats, git status/diff/log and commits, a test runner that finds pytest, npm, dotnet, cargo, go or ctest, multi-file patches with one approval, and background commands for dev servers.

  • Optional online helpers, off by default

    Turn on online research to let every bot search the web and read pages for current docs, versions and error messages, with the sources cited. Or connect your email (IMAP/SMTP over TLS) so it can search, summarize and draft replies. Only you can press Send on an email.

  • Themes and see-through window

    Eleven themes including Midnight blue, Light paper, Terminal green and Amber CRT, or your own colors. Adjustable font size, a text glow slider, and a background opacity slider that lets your desktop show through while text stays crisp.

  • Clean, honest chat

    Replies render Markdown with code blocks and lists, New chat starts fresh, and if a reply claims a change no tool actually made, it says so.

  • Emoji reactions

    React to any message, and the assistant can react back with a fitting emoji.

  • Stop button

    End any reply or tool run instantly. You stay in control of what the assistant does.

System requirements

Minimum

  • Windows 10 or Windows 11, 64-bit (x64)
  • 8 GB of RAM
  • 3 to 6 GB of free disk space for a model
  • Internet once, to download the model

Recommended

  • 16 GB of RAM (runs Qwen3 8B)
  • A graphics card with Vulkan support for much faster replies
  • Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime (built into Windows 11)
  • A microphone for voice input (optional)

Frequently asked questions

Does Offline Coder really work without the internet?

Yes. After the one-time model download (about 2 to 5 GB from Hugging Face), chatting, code search, file edits and voice input all run on your PC. You can unplug the network cable and keep coding. The only network use is the daily update check and engine updates (which you can turn off) plus two optional features that are off until you turn them on: online research and the email connection.

Is my code or chat history sent anywhere?

No. There is no account, no cloud and no telemetry. Your projects, chats, settings and knowledge library stay in the Offline Coder folder on your PC. The app talks only to its own local engine on 127.0.0.1. If you turn on the optional email connection, the app talks to your own mail server over an encrypted connection; your app password is encrypted for your Windows account and never shown to the model.

Is it a private, offline alternative to ChatGPT or Copilot?

For everyday coding help, yes: you get a chat assistant that can read your project, search the code, propose edits and run commands, without sending anything to a cloud service. Local models are smaller than the biggest cloud models, so very large refactors take more steps.

Which AI models does it use?

Open-weight models running on llama.cpp. On first run Offline Coder checks your RAM and graphics card and recommends one: Qwen3 8B with 12 GB of RAM or more (or an 8 GB graphics card), Qwen3 4B Instruct 2507 with 8 GB, and Llama 3.2 3B on smaller PCs. You can switch models at any time in Settings.

What PC do I need?

Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), 8 GB of RAM minimum (16 GB recommended) and 3 to 6 GB of free disk space for a model. A graphics card with Vulkan support makes replies much faster, but a CPU works too. Settings > Re-tune for this PC picks the fastest settings for your hardware.

Can the assistant change my files without asking?

No. Every edit, delete, move and command shows a preview and waits for your approval (except read-only commands you put on a project's auto-approve list). Every change is backed up first, and Settings > Undo last agent change puts the latest one back. The Stop button ends a reply at any time.

Why does Windows SmartScreen show a warning?

Offline Coder is not code-signed yet, so Windows may show "Windows protected your PC" the first time. Click More info, then Run anyway. Only download Offline Coder from its official itch.io page.

How do updates work?

Once a day the app checks this website for a newer version. When one exists, an Update available chip appears and Get update opens the itch.io page, where buyers download new versions from their itch.io library at no extra cost. Nothing is installed automatically.

Can I use it on more than one PC?

Yes. One purchase lets you, as one person, install and use Offline Coder on any computers you own or use. Each person needs their own copy. It is portable: unzip it anywhere, even on a USB drive.

Can the assistant send emails on its own?

No. With the optional email connection on, it can search, read, summarize and draft. A draft appears in the chat with a Send button; nothing is sent until you press it and confirm the recipients, subject and text. Instructions written inside emails are treated as untrusted data and never followed.
